summary.headline: Calendar Intercalation and Jewish Year Types
summary.text: Discussion of solar and lunar calendar intercalation in the Rūmī, Khata'i, Antioch, and Jewish systems, including leap-month placement, crescent or conjunction reckoning, year lengths, and extra, moderate, and deficient years. It also gives the customary weekday restrictions on the Jewish New Year and the 29- or 30-day patterns for Tishrī, Shevat, Nisan, Sivan, Adar, and Marcheshvan.
